title: Literature: The Big Picture
objective: After this level you can explain what literature is and trace its path from spoken myths to the modern novel.
summary: Literature is named for letters (Latin littera), yet it began as spoken stories. It runs from myths told aloud to clay tablets, epics like Gilgamesh and Homer, and the novel.

cards.headline: Literature is named after letters. It started without any.
cards.body: The word comes from the Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet. Yet scholars also speak of oral literature: stories and poems passed on by voice, by people who had no writing at all. So how did literature get from spoken stories to the novel on your shelf?

cards.headline: What counts as literature?
cards.body: In its simplest sense, literature is a body of written works. But the word usually means something narrower: imaginative poems and prose, prized for how well they're made. And it isn't only written. A poem kept alive in people's memories counts as oral literature. Your shopping list, sadly, doesn't count, even though it's written down.

cards.headline: From spoken stories to the novel

events.label: Stories and poems are passed on by voice
Some of the earliest writing appears in Mesopotamia, pressed into clay
Poems about Gilgamesh are written on clay tablets
Homer's epics take shape among singers
The Tale of Genji, often called the first novel

cards.headline: From heroes to people
cards.body: Notice what changes along that line. Gilgamesh and Homer's poems are epics: long poems about heroic deeds. The novel, the newest form here, is an invented story in prose, long and complex. Where the epic lifts its heroes up, the novel often shows life as unheroic, imperfect, even absurd. The epic gave you heroes. The novel gave you people.

mascot.line: If you remember one thing from this level: stories were spoken long before they were written.

cards.headline: Literature: mapped
learned: Spoken stories, clay tablets, epics, then the novel
Epics lift heroes; novels show people

questions.prompt: The word literature comes from the Latin littera, meaning _____.

options.label: a story told out loud
options.rationale: That would be oral literature, not the word's root.

options.label: a bound book of poems
options.rationale: Close in spirit, but littera is a single letter.

questions.explanation: Literature comes from littera, "a letter of the alphabet", which is why it first meant writing.

questions.prompt: How can a poem that was never written down still count as literature?

options.label: It only counts once someone prints it in a book
Only novels count as literature
options.rationale: Poems, epics and myths all count.

options.label: Scholars also recognize oral literature, passed on by voice
Any words at all count, even a shopping list
options.rationale: Literature usually means imaginative, well-made work.

questions.explanation: Literature is usually written, but scholars also speak of oral literature: the stories and poems of peoples without writing.

questions.prompt: Match each word with what it means.
questions.explanation: Littera is Latin for a letter of the alphabet. An epic is a long poem about heroic deeds, and a novel is an invented story in prose.
